items.texte: When you arrive somewhere, say hello with a smile. And goodbye when you leave!
"Please" and "thank you" are magic words: they open all doors.
Take turns sharing your toys. Playing together is even more fun!
In a queue or a game, everyone takes their turn. Being patient shows respect for others.
Wash your hands thoroughly with soap before eating and after using the toilet.
When you've finished playing, put your things away. Your family will thank you!
When you cough or sneeze, put your elbow in front of your mouth.
Wait until everyone has been served before you begin. Always say "please" and "thank you".
Look the person in the eyes when you greet them. A sincere smile is worth a thousand words.
Don't interrupt when someone is speaking. Truly listening is offering a gift.
A sincere and spontaneous thank you creates a strong bond. Don't wait for someone to remind you.
Apologizing takes courage. A heartfelt "I'm sorry" heals a lot.
Knock on the door and wait for a response before entering a room or office.
Hold the door for the person behind you. A small gesture that's always appreciated.
On the bus, give up your seat to an elderly person, a pregnant person, or someone who has difficulty standing.
If someone is alone at recess, offer to play with them.
No need to shout to be heard: a calm voice is better listened to.
Put your phone away during meals and conversations. Your presence is your greatest gift.
Before posting or sending a message, ask yourself: would I say this to someone's face?
Arriving on time shows that you respect other people's time. If you are going to be late, let them know.
To introduce yourself, look at the person, say your first name clearly and smile.
You can disagree without being unpleasant: criticize ideas, never people.
Come closer, say your name and ask, "Do you want to play with me?" That's often how great friendships begin.
Give a sincere and specific compliment: "I love your drawing, the colors are superb!" It's always appreciated.
When a friend is talking to you, look at them, put your screen aside and ask them questions about what they are saying.
A drawing, a kind word, a small homemade gift: small gestures keep friendships alive.
If a friend confides a secret in you, keep it. Unless someone is in danger: then you must talk to a trusted adult.
Remembering someone's first name and using it shows them that they matter to you.
When someone compliments you, a simple thank you is enough. No need to justify yourself.
Little by little, the bird builds its nest. — French proverb
A smile costs nothing and brings much. — Proverb
Treat others as you would like to be treated. — The Golden Rule, present in many cultures
We often need someone smaller than ourselves. — Jean de La Fontaine
There's no point in rushing; you have to leave on time. — Jean de La Fontaine
Unity is strength. — Motto of Belgium
Better late than never. — Proverb
Practice makes perfect. — French proverb
Little streams make great rivers. — French proverb
Patience and time accomplish more than strength or rage. — Jean de La Fontaine
There's no such thing as a bad job. — Proverb
No matter how fast you go, the important thing is not to stop. — Thought attributed to Confucius
What is clearly conceived is clearly expressed. — Nicolas Boileau
One sees clearly only with the heart. What is essential is invisible to the eyes. — Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, The Little Prince
It's never too late to do the right thing. — Proverb
Life is like riding a bicycle: to keep your balance, you must keep moving. — Albert Einstein
Politeness is the art of choosing among one's thoughts. — Quote attributed to Madame de Staël
Politeness is to the mind what grace is to the face. — Voltaire
The secret to success is consistency in purpose. — Benjamin Disraeli
Great things are not accomplished by impulse, but by a series of small things put together. — Vincent van Gogh
Gratitude makes what we have enough for us. — Melody Beattie, American author
We must cultivate our garden. — Voltaire, Candide
He who wants to travel far spares his horse. — Jean Racine
Nothing great has ever been accomplished in the world without passion. — Hegel
Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world. — Nelson Mandela

The future belongs to those who can imagine it, design it, and bring it to fruition. It is not something to be waited for, but something to be created. — Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, engraved on the Museum of the Future in Dubai
The future doesn't wait: it can be imagined, designed, and built today. — From Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Museum of the Future, Dubai
The true wealth of a nation lies in its people, and especially its educated people. — According to Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, founder of the United Arab Emirates
Do not do to others what you would not want done to you. — Confucius
You reap what you sow. — Proverb
Small gifts keep friendships alive. — French proverb
Tell me who your friends are, and I'll tell you who you are. — Proverb
The only way to have a friend is to be one. — Ralph Waldo Emerson
Friendship doubles joys and halves sorrows. — Francis Bacon
If it's difficult, breathe and try again. Every attempt makes you stronger!
You can always ask an adult for help. It's okay not to know.
When you are sad or angry, say it with words. We can help you.
Run, jump, dance: your body loves to move a little every day!
Getting enough sleep helps your brain grow, rest, and retain what you've learned.
Ask questions, read, explore. Curiosity is the driving force behind great discoveries.
Every step counts. Congratulate yourself on the small victories: they build the big ones.
Write your goal down on paper: it helps you remember it and take action!
A big dream comes true with small actions every day. Start with 5 minutes.
All the experts were beginners. The difference? They didn't give up.
A mistake is not a failure: it's information. Ask yourself what you can change next time.
Prepare your things the night before: the morning will be much calmer.
Asking a question doesn't make you look stupid: it's the best way to learn.
Everyone makes mistakes. Forgiving allows you to stay friends and feel lighter.
Be loyal, encourage your friends, and be there when things get tough. That's how you keep your friends for a long time.
In Indian traditions, karma says that every action has consequences. Sow kindness: it often comes back to you.
The people you spend time with influence your habits. Choose friends who encourage you.
Set aside screen-free time to read, move around, and chat. Your brain will thank you.
Doing several things at once wastes time. Focus on one task, then move on to the next.
Sleep, water, movement: these are the basics for being fit and learning well.
Set aside a small portion of every sum received. Small savings become big projects.
